title: Graceful quiescence for model swap and KV checkpointing
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: model hot-swaps during rolling updates cause transient tail-latency spikes and KV-store inconsistencies. Requests inflight across the swap boundary observe mixed checkpoint epochs which leads to increased retried work and KV-contention. Goal: implement a graceful quiesce path for a node during model variant swap that coordinates a lightweight KV checkpoint and a short, bounded quiesce window to drain in-flight batches without introducing high latency or increasing token cost materially. This ticket refactors the scheduler drain path, adds an epoched KV checkpoint API, and wires a canary-safe rollout flag to the routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: Node swap sequence reliably drains inflight continuous-batches within 150ms median added latency on p99-sensitive paths
KV checkpointing completes without blocking normal prefetch work and leaves a verifiable snapshot marker visible to the reconciler
No increased 5xx rate during canary model swap in internal staging for 100k requests/hour for 30 minutes
E2E rollout smoke (canary->gradual) shows <=5% median latency regression and p99 increase bounded to <10% compared to baseline
tasks: Design: document quiesce protocol and epoched KV checkpoint contract (Confluence)
Implement: lightweight KV checkpoint writer that emits snapshot metadata but avoids full compaction
Refactor: scheduler drain hook to signal continuous-batcher preemption and await safe completion or timeout
Integrate: routing flag for model-swap graceful mode and canary gating
Tests: unit tests for checkpoint metadata and integration test under load with chaos injection
Run: staged canary in staging, capture perf metrics, iterate on timeout tuning
notes: Decision: prefer non-blocking checkpoint writer (append-only snapshot metadata) over stop-the-world checkpoint to minimize tail latency
Tradeoff: short quiesce windows may leave some inflight requests to be retried; we picked 250ms hard cap for safety, tuned down from initial 500ms after microbenchmarks
Benchmarks: synthetic workload (seq_len=1024, batch target 16) shows quiesce+checkpoint path adds +12% median token latency and +8% p99 when using appendable snapshot; acceptable for canary tier
Follow-ups: expose quiesce timeout as a runtime-config and add traceback logs on preempted batches for postmortem analysis
